meta.Zones covered: Children's play area | pathways & tree belt
meta.Annotated videos: Two MP4 files in this folder, one per clip

headlineFindings: Bare, hard-packed ground is the dominant defect. It averages 30.5% of frame in the play area and 21.2% on the pathways, while lawn cover is only 2.4% and 8.0% respectively - the ground plane has essentially failed in both zones.
watering scores worst in the play area at 46.9/100, driven by that bare ground. This matches the site record of widespread dry patches.
Cleanliness is poor throughout - loose ground debris covers 20-24% of open ground, worst on the pathways at 46.7/100. Discrete litter is visible on the play-area surface in the footage.

The play area is well equipped - slides, climbing frames, a multi-play unit with coloured canopies and swings were all detected (736 equipment records). Their paint-integrity scores are the evidence for the site note of getting worse paint and broken units; check the lowest scorers in the anomaly register.
facilities is weaker on the pathways (65.4) than in the play area (79.3), consistent with the site record of poor pavement condition.
Vehicles were detected inside the park boundary (44 records) - the highest count of any park surveyed so far.
Tree tree cover and shrubs are reasonably healthy; the trees are not the problem here, the ground under them is.

recommendations.Category: A1 Plantation & Green Cover / A3 Irrigation
recommendations.Finding: The ground plane has failed in both zones - bare hard-packed earth at 30.5% and 21.2% of frame with lawn cover at 2.4% and 8.0%. watering scores 46.9 in the play area.
recommendations.Recommended action: Reinstate ground cover as a programme, not a patch repair: decompact, regrade, re-turf and install watering that actually reaches the play area. Under play equipment, install a proper impact-absorbing surface rather than bare earth.

recommendations.Finding: The site record notes a broken swing, broken tiles on gym equipment and getting worse signboard paint. The detector finds and scores the equipment but cannot itself assert structural damage.
recommendations.Recommended action: Physically inspect every play and gym unit; use the anomaly register to prioritise the lowest paint-integrity scores. Make any broken unit safe immediately - this is a children's play area.

recommendations.Finding: 44 vehicle detections inside the park boundary, the highest of any park surveyed.
recommendations.Recommended action: Establish why vehicles are routinely inside the green boundary and enforce restrictions or formalise a controlled access route.

recommendations.Finding: Loose ground debris covers 20-24% of open ground and discrete litter is visible on the play surface.
recommendations.Recommended action: Daily housekeeping in the play area; increase sweeping on the pathways and check bin provision and emptying frequency.

recommendations.Finding: Pathway facilities scores 65.4, notably below the play area, matching the site note of poor pavement condition.
recommendations.Recommended action: Survey the path network; patch and resurface the worst segments and reset displaced edging.

recommendations.Finding: No class exists for: broken equipment, signboards, gazebo / pergola, streetlights, dustbins, boundary wall as distinct from kerb, or the waterway condition recorded on site.
recommendations.Recommended action: Confirm which matter most for the DDA report. 'Broken' is genuinely hard from imagery; a low-altitude pass over the play equipment would serve better than a detector.

recommendations.Finding: The site record mentions a waterway that is not clear and a gazebo, neither substantially covered by these two clips.
recommendations.Recommended action: Fly the waterway and the gazebo area to capture that evidence.

recommendations.Finding: No .SRT telemetry accompanied these clips, and this is a single-date capture.
recommendations.Recommended action: Export flight logs with the video to unlock geo-tagging; repeat the flight path later for change detection against this baseline.
